Alex — thanks for the note and sorry for the confusion.

Short answer: Chili Piper should convert to the browser's locale, but we've seen a cutover bug where browser locale or cached cookies cause the widget to default to PT/UTC for some EU customers after DST changes. Workaround is to either: 1) append a TZ param to the ChiliPiper deep link, or 2) send a manual ICS with an explicit TZID field (recommended for reliability).

I've created a manual invite (attached) using Europe/London TZ headers and included two concrete slots so you can pick the one that works:
- Thu 18 Jun 2025 19:00 BST (18:00 UTC) — 30 min demo + 15 min QA
- Fri 19 Jun 2025 17:00 BST (16:00 UTC) — 30 min demo + 15 min QA

I'm copying Soojin (Solutions) to confirm the call dial-in and Naomi to add a calendar-friendly subject line and attendee list.

Attaching: demo-invite-LON.ics (explicit TZID=Europe/London) and a quick screenshot showing the Chili Piper widget where we reproduce the PT default (tz-screenshot.png).

If you accept one of the invites, I'll send a confirmation and a short agenda.

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks for looping me in. Quick notes from the solutions side:

- Confirmed: Chili Piper deep-links sometimes inherit the server default when the browser locale is ambiguous during DST transitions. We have a short-term fix: add &tz=Europe/London (or &tz=America/Los_Angeles) to the deep link which forces conversion.
- Long-term: we'll propose a UX guard that shows a timezone banner on the widget when DST boundaries are near.

For now, Jordan's manual ICS is the safest path. The ICS I created includes this header so calendar apps interpret it correctly:
BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
TZID:Europe/London
X-LIC-LOCATION:Europe/London
...
END:VTIMEZONE

Jordan — if Alex accepts, I'll join the call for the first 10 minutes to run through integration touchpoints and then hand off to Naomi for billing/next steps.

Alex — feel free to accept either invite; if you prefer a different time zone representation (e.g., show UTC in the subject line) we can do that too.

Cheers,
